newsitem.title: CHINA: Bank of China urges defaulter to repay US$16 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China urges defaulter to repay US$16 mln.

text.p: The Bank of China (BOC) has said it will sue a Shenzhen-listed company if it continues to delay repayment of a loan, according to a bank statement said Thursday.

Searainbow Group Co Ltd, a chemical fibre maker based in southern Hainan province, had delayed repayment to the BOC of US$15.88 million in principal and interest, said the statement in Thursday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The loans, guaranteed by five domestic institutions, were made in July 1993, the statement said. No details of the terms were given.
"The serious violation of the agreement by Searainbow and the five guarantors has destroyed their images and creditworthinesses," the BOC's statement said.
"The debtors and gurantors must carry out their duty in 30 days ... otherwise, the bank will pursue the loans according to law," it said.
Bad loans have been one of the main problems haunting Chinese state banks, which are trying to limit non-performing loans by strengthening checks on financial risks.
A statement by Searainbow in the same newspaper said it used the loans to finance a chemical fibre project and it was unable to repay on time because the investment was a failure.
"It is difficult for our company to repay the loan to the Bank of China," it said. "Our company is negotiating with related parties to look for methods."
Trading in Searainbow's domestic currency A shares was suspended on Thursday morning pending the statement, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said.
The share closed at 9.71 yuan on Wednesday.
